activities.sharedMaterialsRationale: The 4–6 and 7–9 material lists are intentionally identical and physically sufficient. This is not evidence of a duplicated experiment: 4–6 holds length at 12 cm and compares stationary/held-bent/released states, separating visible motion from heard sound; 7–9 actually changes free length through 12/8/8/12 cm, repeats in reverse order, holds listening position and approximately 3 mm deflection comparable, and records pitch separately from loudness. Its independent variable, comparison design, repetition and interpretation differ from the younger protocol. Their common ruler/book/measurement tools are legitimate reusable apparatus. No unnecessary item or cosmetic wording change is required to manufacture material-list uniqueness. This explicit operational review supports an exception to exact-material-array duplication checks, not an exception for whole-protocol or cosmetic duplication.
